1.why: In /api/verify the reset record’s accountKey must match session.recoveryAccountKey before the code is accepted.

2.why: A reset code is bound to one accountKey and fails verification on any session whose recoveryAccountKey does not match.

3.why: Password reset only clears flags on the current session; other existing sessions in the Map are not invalidated or version-checked.

4.why: Bun is started with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, though the exact TLS version is left to runtime defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via bcrypt; protection is hashing rather than encryption, but algorithms are appropriate.

6.why: There is no real mailer; simulated recovery responses use generic copy and do not embed extra private patient fields.

7.why: Identifiers/tokens are format-validated server-side and the UI renders with textContent/DOM APIs, not untrusted HTML.

8.why: recoveryLink is a same-origin relative path (/recovery-link?token=...); no open external redirect is implemented.

9.why: No email HTML templates consume user input; demo delivery only returns a controlled code/link payload.

10.why: API errors are generic, but demo activity logs and JSON fields (mockRecoveryCode, mockMfaCode) intentionally expose tokens.

11.why: Password is bcrypt-hashed at rest, yet MFA_CODE and a default password hash are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The fixed demo account helena.demo@hospital.test with known mock password hash and MFA code 246810 is accepted.

13.why: actionAllowed/rateAllowed throttle recovery, verify, login, password, MFA, and related actions per session and source.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same “If this account can receive…” message whether or not the identifier is approved.

15.why: Codes come from randomBytes(32) base64url, are stored hashed, single-use/expiry-bound, and tied to a specific accountKey.
